name: Suba Hotels Ltd
tagline: A fast-growing, high-ROE mid-scale hotel aggregator on the NSE SME board - but a brand-light, franchise-heavy model with no pricing power and 1.06x leverage; a good small business, not a 10x thesis.
business_overview: Mid-scale Indian hotel chain operating a mixed model - owned, managed, revenue-share, lease and franchised - with a large managed/franchised portfolio (reported ~1,500+ hotels in the network). FY25 revenue Rs 79.98 Cr, +51% YoY. Listed on NSE SME in 2026 at a ~46% premium (15x+ oversubscribed IPO). Seeded as an external lead from X triage (@BeatTheStreet10, untrusted) citing highest-ever revenue and rapid hotel-count growth.
fundamentals_table: +51% to Rs 79.98 Cr FY25; ~48% avg for 3 years
D/E ~1.06 - notable leverage for an asset-light model
fundamentals_narrative: Suba shows strong headline metrics - ~32% ROE, ~36% ROCE, ~50% revenue CAGR - and an asset-light aggregation model that can add hotels quickly. But mid-scale hotel branding at this size has essentially no pricing power; it competes with OYO, Treebo, FabHotels and dozens of regional chains, franchisee churn is a structural risk, and D/E of ~1.06 is high for a model that is supposed to be capital-light (suggesting the 'owned/lease' leg carries the balance sheet). Revenue base is tiny (Rs 80 Cr) and the listing is on the SME board.
technical_read: NSE SME, listed 2026; traded ~Rs 104 to ~Rs 200 post-listing. No meaningful weekly/monthly structure.
sentiment_summary: No ValuePickr thread (topic_slug null); search returned only generic strategy and Mumbai-meetup threads. Assessment is web/filings-based. Only external signal is an untrusted-X mention (@BeatTheStreet10).
community_signal: No trusted-user activity. External lead only: @BeatTheStreet10 (untrusted X triage) flagged record revenue (~Rs 115.89 Cr cited), 100+ hotels and ~45% growth.
bse_notes: No SEBI / fraud action found. Recent SME listing - limited disclosure history. Watch the split between owned/leased vs pure franchised revenue (drives the real margin and balance-sheet profile) and franchisee-retention / same-hotel RevPAR trends.
bull_case: Asset-light aggregation lets it add hotels to the network quickly
Indian mid-scale / branded-budget hospitality is under-penetrated and formalising
Small base - room to grow revenue for years
bear_case: Brand-light mid-scale model - little to no pricing power; commoditised segment (OYO / Treebo / FabHotels / regional chains)
D/E ~1.06 - high leverage for a supposedly asset-light model
Franchisee churn and inconsistent quality are structural risks to a network model
Rs 80 Cr revenue base on the NSE SME board - liquidity and disclosure limits
Single source is an untrusted X account
Hospitality is cyclical; the current up-cycle is not a structural multi-year driver at this scale
verdict_headline: Fast-growing, high-ROE SME hotel aggregator with no pricing power and real leverage - a decent small business, not a 10x/100x candidate. thesis_fit 'neither', conviction Low-Medium.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind weak (Indian mid-scale hospitality up-cycle is real but cyclical, not a structural multi-year driver at this scale), tam yes (branded-budget hotel aggregation TAM is large), moat no (no pricing power, weak brand, franchisee-churn risk, crowded field), valuation weak (~25-30x earnings, D/E ~1.06) -> score 2.0
Score 2.0-2.5 with no valuation-yes and no un-ignorable-growth carve-out that survives the missing moat + leverage: label stays 'neither'
Conviction Low-Medium: fast growth and strong ratios keep it off Low, but the absence of a moat, the leverage on an 'asset-light' model, and an untrusted single source cap it there
